subject: Climate & Environment
title: Passive House Design
description: A 60-second lesson on Passive House Design.

hook.text: A Passive House uses up to 90% less energy for heating and cooling than a standard building.

buildup.text: The design uses super-thick insulation, airtight construction, and heat-recovery ventilation.

discovery.text: Triple-glazed windows and strategic orientation capture solar heat in winter and block it in summer.

twist.text: The extra construction cost is only about 10 to 15% — paid back through energy savings within years.

climax.text: Over 65,000 Passive House buildings exist worldwide. The standard works in every climate.

punchline.text: The greenest energy is the energy a building never needs.

quiz.question: How much less energy does a Passive House use for heating and cooling?

details.summary: Passive House is a building standard that reduces energy demand by up to 90 percent through superinsulation, airtight construction, triple glazing, and heat-recovery ventilation. Buildings meeting the standard require minimal active heating or cooling even in extreme climates.
details.whyItMatters: Passive House demonstrates that extreme energy efficiency is achievable in any climate. Scaling this approach could eliminate a huge share of building-sector emissions.
takeaways: Passive House buildings use up to 90 percent less energy
Superinsulation and airtightness are core principles
Heat-recovery ventilation provides fresh air without heat loss

faq.question: What is heat-recovery ventilation?
faq.answer: An HRV system exhausts stale indoor air while transferring up to 90 percent of its heat to incoming fresh air. This maintains indoor air quality without opening windows and prevents the heat loss that conventional ventilation causes in winter.

faq.question: Is Passive House more expensive to build?
faq.answer: Premium costs range from 5 to 15 percent above conventional construction. However, dramatically lower energy bills mean most Passive Houses pay back the extra cost within 5 to 15 years, and occupants enjoy superior comfort and air quality from day one.
